Core Notes
Core System

CN1.) For all text field entry and keypad, when pressing the backspace button will remove a single character with each press. Press and hold of the backspace button for >500ms will perform fast backspace. Long press will remove a single character at an increment of 200ms util the button is released. If the button remains pressed after all characters are removed, rejection tone will be played and the backspace button will be greyed out.

CN1.1) When editing a text field (for example: profile username), dis ay the current text string with the cursor at the end of the text. The saved text is available for the user to edit by placing the cursor anywhere within the text. If the text is ghosted, to be defined in the feature logic, the cursor will default to the beginning of the text and the text will be cleared once the user enters new characters. Exiting without saving will not result in an update to the text field.
CN2.) VR will overtake status bar.
CN3.) Head unit features including but not limited to apps, settings, main menu bar categories, and main menu category tabs a-e dependent on vehicle configuration.
CN4.) Brand Names: FCA Brand Names will not be translated.

CN5.) Truncation: If a text string is too long to fit in the text field, truncate the string (displaying as many full words as possible) and put"..." at the end so that it fits within the given text field.
CN6.) Content tiles (ex. apps and controls) within a tab or drawer remain the same size regardless of the amount of content within the screen. Content tiles are left justified.
CN7.) Category Tabs: The Head Unit can have a maximum of 6 tabs in a Category or App used for navigation of the section.

CN8.) Reconfiguring Disabled Icons: Icons that are disabled in areas that allow for reconfiguration should maintain long press behavior so they can be reconfigured. Short press behavior should be ignored or provide feedback as specified by the applicable requirements h the logic and flow.
CN9.) Variable Icons: Some icons may be variable base on brand, vehicle line, region, or configuration. See PDQ graphics and Feature Logic and Flow for details.
CN10.) List Types: Lists include both line item lists and tile-based lists.
CN11.) (R1 LOW ONLY) If an app is not available due to a delay in loading, grey out the icon in all applicable locations. If the user presses the greyed out icon, show PU1285.
CN12.) Apps that are deleted by the user (third party downloaded apps for example) should delete from all areas of the system for the profile they were deleted from.
Audio
CNA1.) Tones: Play appropriate audible confirmation where indicated. Refer to CFTS019 for sound definitions.
CNA2.) Audio ducking: While Text Message and Apps TTS are playing, the audio of the currently playing audio source will be muted (if Media it will also be paused).
Lockouts

CNL1.) Lockout while in Motion: If a feature or function is locked out while the vehicle is in motion, its access point shall be greyed out, and provide the "Function not available while vehicle is in motion" popup (PU0091) along with rejection tone. An exception to this rule is the messaging button for vehicles with embedded cell, where the messaging button remains available while the vehicle is in motion to provide haptic access to VR SMS dictation (see Phone Logic and Flow).

CNL2.) If a speller is blocked, the button to access to that speller is greyed out while in motion. If the speller is already up while the vehicle is in motion, all speller buttons are greyed out except for close and go/enter. Text shown in previous keyboard area stating "Keyboard unavailable while vehicle is in motion. Press 'OK' to accept current entry". Replace OK in these instructions with label of OK/Enter button.

AO7.) User will not be placed in mute status if turning the volume down to zero. The music will not be paused.

AO8.) If receiving an incoming call and the user presses mute on the hard control or in the touch screen, the ringtone will be muted and the Mute button will be highlighted. If the user answers the call, the call will not be muted.
AO9.) Head unit will mute when launching app via Off Road+ or SRT (ADR) hard control from Power Button Off state (idle mode).

User can swipe lists up/down or left/right

(ex: do not show empty space as seen in example photo)_x000D_\n (image: %E5%9C%96%E7%89%87_1674717913.png)
User Action:
For vertical lists:

Scrolling Down:_x000D_\nWith one finger, user performs a simultaneous press-hold. While the finger is held down, upward movement of finger will drag/swipe list upward, which will show lower items in the list. Releasing finger does not select an item. A list item is only selected once it is pressed. If the user stops scrolling and presses the up or down page arrow, they will be taken to the previous or next page, respectively (ex: if user gesture scrolls to page three and then presses the down arrow, they will be taken to page four.) If user stops scrolling with finger and turns knob, list will move down or up ( (dependent on direction of knob turn) one item/line at a time. Cursor will move from top or bottom line to the next line in the list.

Scrolling Up:_x000D_\nWith one finger, user performs a simultaneous press-hold. While the finger is held down, downward movement of finger will drag/swipe list downward, which will show items higher in list. Releasing finger does not select an item. A list item is only selected once� is pressed. If the user stops scrolling and presses the up or down page arrow, they will be taken to the previous or next page, respectively (ex: if user gesture scrolls to page three and then presses the down arrow, they will be taken to page four.) if user stops scrolling with finger and turns knob, list will move down or up (dependent on direction of knob turn) one item/line at a time. Cursor will move from top or bottom line to the next line in the list.
Do not show highlight while scrolling list, or in case of a fast press, or while flick scrolling, or performing a roll stop.

Press Event Core Description

PECO1.) Active areas actions are triggered at the Button RELEASE event. Active areas' actions are cancelled if the finger is released outside of the area. This is valid for all the active areas of the display.
PECD2.) If button has long press capability, once long press functionality begins, there should be auditory feedback (single touchscreen beep).
PECD3.) Long Press: When long press behavior is applicable, pressing the button for more than 500ms, will increment/decrement 1 step every 200ms unless otherwise specified.
PECD4.) Fan speed bars, volume sliders, and bass/mid/treble should allow the user to simply slide their finger up/down to change the setting as well as press directly on the desired setting.
PECO5.) All touchscreen buttons should have an auditory beep associated with activation -> auditory feedback, unless user turns off touchscreen beep.

PECD6.) Buttons and tabs will be labeled with the first letter of each word being capitalized and the rest lowercase. Not Applicable to Acronyms. The Main rv1enu Bar will be displayed with an Icon and Text below.
PECO7.) Disabled Buttons: If a button is not available it should be greyed out and a rejection tone played (refer to CFTS019 for appropriate tone).
PECO8.) Selected Buttons: When a button is selected it will be highlighted.
PECD9.) Button States: Buttons in the Head Unit can have 3 states: Active, Not Active, and Disabled. Graphical states will be defined by PDO.
Pressable Area Core Behavior

PACB1.) Visual feedback of active area's touch is linked to the PRESS event. It is valid for all active areas with or without long press functionality._x000D_\n (image: %E5%9C%96%E7%89%87_461991229.png)

PACB1.1.) Visual feedback associated to the PRESSED state of an active area is composed by:_x000D_
•    Changing the color of button graphics (text labels and/or icon) applying the branded highlight color._x000D_
•    Showing an additional graphical feedback applying the branded shape. This element has to be positioned centered-aligned to the button area. _x000D_
This strategy is valid for all the active areas of the display (Buttons, Main Category bar) except lists (for the list management see specific page), Status Bar (highlight of the entire pressable area, same as a list), and draggable areas.
PACB1.2.) Draggable areas do not display any pressed state's visual feedback, just perform the action (e.g. fill segments with highlight for audio setting options values)

PACB2.) Pressable areas should have at least 12mm (recommendable for most controls) even if the graphic content (labels, icons, letters) do not cover the entire pressable region. Also, a pressable area should never be smaller than its correspondent graphical asset. Any pressable region must be fully centralized on the correspondent graphical asset.

PACB3.) Adjacent buttons should have a 3mm gap between their pressable areas (even though the graphics show them closer than 3mm). This rule does not affect continuous draggable areas such as EQ and fan scrubbers. The scrubber used in list screens requires a 40 pixel tall by 45 pixel wide active area (larger than the graphical area) that is centered on the center of the face of the scrubber. In order to make the scrubber grabbable from the top and bottom of the scrubber range, do not implement the 3mm non-touchable gap between the scrubber and the page up/down buttons. Finally, for the song progress and instant replay scrubbers, increase the touchable area by increasing the active height to 32 pixels, centered on the middle of the scrubber face. The active width of this scrubber can remain the displayed pixels.
Reconfiguration Behavior
RB1.) Pressing and holding on any icon in the radio results in a larger duplicate "ghost icon" to aid the user in reconfiguration.

RB2.) Drag to Reorder (Status Bar and Media Sources in Pinned Sources Bank): If the user presses and holds on an icon and a "ghost icon" is created, they can drop the icon over another icon. The new icon will take the place and the original icon will transition bad< into it's place in the drawer or tab.

RB2.1.) Drag to Reorder (Horne Screen Shortcuts, Media Sources in Source Drawer, and Main Menu): If the user presses and holds on an icon and a "ghost icon" is created, they can drop the icon over another icon. The new icon will displace the original icon and the icons will shift to the right for the Main Menu and will reorder for the Shortcuts Widget and Media Sources.

RB3.) Button Release during Reordering: When the user presses and holds an icon and creates a "ghost icon" if they drop the con outside of an available drop zone, it will return to its original location and no changes will be made.
List Management

LM1.) When the user selects an item in a list by pressing on the screen, the visual feedback of list item's touch is an highlight of the list item area. No additional graphical feedback is displayed. Also Audio Setting list and Track list splitview follow this general rule.

LM3.) Scroll bar+ up/ down arrows (or left/right for horizontal scrolling) are only presented if list items exceed maximum number of items that can be displayed at once. The maximum number of list entries presented on the screen varies. Use scroll knob to move cursor one item down/ up in list per turn. Use arrows to move one page down/up (or right/left) per press. Scrubber indicates position in the list. Use scrubber to quickly move up/ down the list. User can press scrubber to move list position; if user initially presses scrubber area outside of scrubber, ignore the press. Continue to track position and move handle while user holds finger down on the scrubber. If user moves outside scrubber area without releasing continue sliding function until finger is released. If user releases finger within scrubber area, keep last valid scrubber position and deactivate sliding function. Long press is to advance one page per 200ms. When applicable a dynamic scroll bar will be available which illustrates where the user is in the list. The dynamic scroll bar should only appear when there is more than one page of content. For 7" only, dynamic scroll bar will appear on the screen while user is interacting with the list and disappear after 5 seconds. This scroll bar is not interactive but exists to show the user where they are within a list.

LM4.) For alphabetical lists (e.g. Media song lists and mobile phone book) ten pages or longer, show popup next to scrubber (similar behavior to temp scrubber popup) with the first letter or number of the entry corresponding to that scrubber position (excluding "The "or artists). Use"!#;" (exclamation mark, pound, and semicolon) in the popup for the symbol portion of the list. As possible, update the list view while in this alpha-popup mode; the highest priority is to update the active letter as the user slides the scrubber up and down. Provide only available letters (present just the base capital letter for all versions of the letter) and numbers to the user (as well as !#;). Once the user releases the scrubber, remove the letter popup and maintain the final list position.

LM5.) If back button is pressed when the user is at the top level of a list browsing hierarchy, user is taken back to the main screen mode of the mode from which they entered the list from (see Last Mode notes). Category sorting does not qualify as a level in a list browsing hierarchy. Example of levels in a list browsing hierarchy, where the "Genre" category is the TOP level, and the album, "Dark Side of the Moon" is he BOTTOM level: Genre> Rock> Pink Floyd> Dark Side of the Moon.

LM6.) Alphabetical lists order should have the following priority: symbols, letters, numbers. The only exception to the alphabetization is for artists lists in Media, which ignores "The " before an artist name when alphabetizing.
LM6.1.) Symbols should be ordered by their Unicode value (with the exception that space is first).
LM6.2.) Numbers should be ordered by their Unicode value.

LM6.3.) Letters should be alphabetized in a two-state method. First, alphabetize by the stripped down version of the letters, i.e. convert international and capital letters to the lower case letter base version of that letter (e.g. Ö becomes o). Next, if there are two or more entries that have the exact same base entry, use the letter's non-stripped Unicode value to disambiguate the order. For example, if the database has motorhead, Motorhead, and Mötorhead, they would all have the same base version (motorhead). The unicode value of the first character (m vs M) would place Motorhead and Mötorhead ahead of motorhead. Next, between Motorhead and Mötorhead, the unicode value of o is less than ö and so Motorhead would appear before Mötorhead. The final list order would be Motorhead, Mötorhead, and then motorhead.

LM7.) Empty Lists: For all lists, display 'No items' as first list item if list is empty; exceptions: presets will display 'HOLD to Save' for empty presets, Phone Browsing will display 'No contacts in phonebook' and Recent calls will display 'No Recent Calls'. This applies to lists that will become populated at some point, not lists that are empty based on configuration. If a list is empty based on configuration and will never be populated with content, do not show it.
LM8.) Whenever a list takes too long to display, show "Please Wait..." popup with animated dots.

LM9.) List scrolling is one item at a time, not one page at a time. For clockwise turning of the knob, the cursor box moves tom the top of the list (position #1), to position #2, then #3, to the bottom of the list, and then adds one item at a time to last position, scrolling the other list items upward. For counter-clockwise motion, if not already in position #1 (ie. Moves from position #4, to 3, to 2, to 1), then scrolls items downward. If item is greyed out in a list, cursor would jump over that item to the next viable option. If whole list is greyed out, cursor would not be shown. If user puts vehicle in motion while on greyed out list item, cursor does not move.
LM10.) While in lists, have the final page full. Bring items from the next to last page to the final page and have the final item(s) at the bottom of the list. Lists can have a maximum of 6 items.

LM11.) List item selection: The user can select a list item either by pressing on the screen or by pressing the ENTER button inside the scroll knob. When selecting an item in a list, it should be momentarily highlighted before moving to the next screen.

LM12.) When in sub-browsing menus, using the back button takes the user back to the previous list screen. The user should be positioned in the list on the item which they selected to enter that sub-browsing menu, not at the top of the list. While in any list, the Back button will be available. If the user is on the top page of the menu they will be taken out of the list and back to the main screen they were at before enteri1g the list.
